name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Abuse of command-line and scripting interpreters to execute commands, scripts or binaries.

name: PowerShell
description: Use of PowerShell to run commands, download payloads or execute scripts, often obfuscated or encoded.

name: Windows Command Shell
description: Use of cmd.exe to run commands or batch scripts.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
description: A malicious file delivered as an email attachment that the user is lured into opening.

name: User Execution: Malicious File
description: The user opens a delivered file (document, archive, executable) which starts the malicious chain.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Downloading tools or payloads from an external system into the compromised environment.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
description: Adding a program to a Run/RunOnce key or Startup folder so it executes at logon.

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
description: Creating or modifying a Windows scheduled task to run code on a schedule or at logon.

name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
description: Installing or modifying a Windows service so a payload runs with SYSTEM privileges and survives reboot.

name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
description: Reading the memory of lsass.exe to extract credential material.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Encoding, encrypting or otherwise obscuring payloads and commands to evade analysis and detection.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
description: Using mshta.exe to execute HTA files or inline script through a trusted signed binary.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Regsvr32
description: Using regsvr32.exe to load and run code, including remote scriptlets, via a trusted signed binary.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
description: Using rundll32.exe to execute DLL exports or scripts through a trusted signed binary.

name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Using SMB admin shares (ADMIN$, C$) with valid credentials to move laterally and execute remotely, e.g. PsExec.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
description: Using WMI to execute commands locally or on remote hosts.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
description: Command-and-control traffic blended into HTTP/HTTPS.

name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
description: Deleting dropped files or tools to remove traces of activity.

name: BITS Jobs
description: Abuse of Background Intelligent Transfer Service jobs to download or execute payloads.

name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Logon Script (Windows)
description: Adding a logon script via UserInitMprLogonScript or similar so code runs at user logon.

name: Impair Defenses: Disable Windows Event Logging
description: Disabling or modifying Windows event logging to hide activity.

name: Modify Registry
description: Modifying the Windows registry to hide configuration changes or impair defenses.

name: OS Credential Dumping: NTDS
description: Accessing or copying the Active Directory NTDS.dit database to extract credentials.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Attempting to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material.

name: OS Credential Dumping: DCSync
description: Abusing Directory Replication Service to simulate a domain controller and pull password data.

name: Process Injection
description: Injecting code into processes to evade defenses and elevate or hide execution.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution
description: Using signed Microsoft binaries to proxy execution of malicious payloads.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution: InstallUtil
description: Using InstallUtil.exe to execute .NET assemblies and bypass application controls.

name: XSL Script Processing
description: Using XSL stylesheets to execute scripts embedded in or referenced by XML.

name: File and Directory Permissions Modification
description: Modifying file or directory permissions or ownership to evade defenses or enable access.
